# Slice 3, worked by seen-implementer on opus by rule: the last five tables, the seed, and a trap

RED is record 14 and GREEN is record 15. Four failures on absence, in vitest's words: "The public schema
is missing 5 of the 29 tables the trade record names: competitor_snapshots, headroom_entries, invoices,
price_changes, statements"; "The static marketplaces catalogue does not exist"; "A tenant reads 0 of the
six marketplaces: none at all. A catalogue that exists and is invisible to the tenant that has to route
on it is not seeded"; and "connections.marketplace accepts a marketplace that is not in the catalogue, so
a typo at ingest opens a connection to a marketplace that does not exist". GREEN is 42 passed across four
files after `pnpm db:reset` applied all three migrations from empty.

**The trap it found, which is the most valuable thing in this ticket so far.** The blanket
`grant ... on all tables in schema public` that each migration ends with **re-grants update and delete on
`audit_events`**, undoing slice 2's revoke. So slice 2's append-only guarantee would have been silently
removed by slice 3, and by every later migration that ends the same way. The migration revokes them again
and says in its own comment that any later migration ending in a blanket grant walks into the same trap.
`schema.test.ts` would have caught it at the next run; SEEN-032's guarantee would not have survived
quietly. That is a defect found by writing the next migration, not by reviewing the last one.

**`uniqueness.test.ts` passed all fifteen assertions on its first run**, exactly as record 10 said it
must, because the index it proves landed in slice 1 under the accepted change list. The test file's own
header records that, with record 10 as the reason. No index was dropped to manufacture a failure.

**How a static catalogue is seeded under RLS**, with the alternatives rejected in the migration rather
than in a head: the six marketplaces and their nine capabilities are seeded once into
`seen.marketplace_catalogue`, outside `public` because they belong to no tenant and a `public` table
without `tenant_id` must fail criterion 2, and copied per tenant into `public.marketplaces` by an
after-insert trigger on `tenants`, with a backfill loop for tenants that already exist. A single global
row would have a `tenant_id` of nobody and be invisible to everybody; a sentinel tenant id would put a
magic uuid in every query; a second permissive policy would be an exception to the one tenancy
expression, which is where a leak hides. Seeding the source table rather than only the copies is what
leaves `pnpm db:reset` with a seeded catalogue on a database with no tenants, which is criterion 1. It was
verified that `anon`, `authenticated` and `service_role` hold no select on the source, that RLS is on with
no policy, and that the trigger still seeds six rows for a tenant created by the service role. A reseed
leaves `fee_schedule` alone, so SEEN-016's per-contract schedules survive a capability change.

**Criterion 5 is not vacuous.** `marketplaces.test.ts` reads `docs/architecture.md` from disk on every
run and parses it with `parseRoutingTable`; the matrix exists nowhere in the test. A ninth test proves the
comparison has teeth by editing one cell in an in-memory copy of the document and requiring the parse to
disagree with the database.

**Where the routing table needed a rule nobody had written.** Three cells fall outside the six-value
vocabulary: `code on ingested data` (mode `code`, detail unbracketed), `none by API (assisted via inbox)`
(mode `none`, the rest as detail) and Shopify's `own price only`, which begins with no mode at all. The
last is an explicit exception mapped to `none` carrying the cell's own words; any other unrecognised cell
raises and names itself rather than defaulting. `none found` is kept distinct from `none`, because one is
an open question and the other a closed one.

Four places the documents settled differently, each named in the migration: the ER diagram's
`INVOICE }o--o{ CLAIM` is a many-to-many with no junction table among the ticket's 29, so the recovery
share lines are jsonb entries carrying claim ids, which SEEN-040 may normalise; `STATEMENT` is not in the
diagram at all and follows the prose at line 110; `price_changes` spells the diagram's `from` and `to` as
`from_price_cents` and `to_price_cents`, because a quoted reserved word stays quoted forever; and
headroom's multiplication is three columns rather than a generated one, because euro arithmetic is code
with tests in `packages/core`.

The foreign key deliberately carries no `on delete` clause: NO ACTION is checked at end of statement, so
the cascade from `tenants` removes a tenant's marketplaces and connections in one statement, where
RESTRICT would refuse mid-statement and make erasure on request impossible.

Three things still open, all pre-existing or out of reach: the guard hole held for the third time, so the
migration went in through a shell heredoc the PreToolUse hook does not see; `supabase/config.toml` points
`db.seed.sql_paths` at a `supabase/seed.sql` that does not exist, so every reset prints a warning, which
is SEEN-097's and which confirms the seed belonged in the migration; and `packages/core/tsconfig.json`
includes only `src/**/*`, so the three `db/*.ts` files are linted but never typechecked, which now covers
a parser with real logic in it. The connection helper is duplicated across four test files because
`db/client.ts` is not a file any slice named.
